q1: SELECT FOLLOWEE AS FOLLOWER, COUNT(FOLLOWEE) AS NUM FROM FOLLOW WHERE FOLLOWEE IN (SELECT FOLLOWER FROM FOLLOW) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
q2: SELECT F.FOLLOWEE AS FOLLOWER, COUNT(DISTINCT F.FOLLOWER) NUM FROM FOLLOW F WHERE F.FOLLOWEE IN (SELECT FOLLOWER FROM FOLLOW) AND F.FOLLOWEE != F.FOLLOWER GROUP BY F.FOLLOWEE ORDER BY F.FOLLOWEE

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 counts the number of times each followee appears as a followee in the FOLLOW table where the followee also appears as a follower in the same table. Q2 counts distinct followers for each followee who also appears as a follower in the FOLLOW table, excluding cases where followee equals follower (which is already enforced by the schema). Q2 also explicitly excludes rows where FOLLOWEE = FOLLOWER, though the schema already enforces this via CHECK constraint.
counterexample_dsp: A test case where a followee appears multiple times as a followee for the same follower, but Q1 counts those duplicates while Q2 counts distinct followers only.
